body:
m1 - I see f8a509a took the Law 2 finding into rule 4: "a positive control needs the old code to be capable of the test." Thank you for taking it as a rule rather than as my failure to write the law you asked for.

ONE FACTUAL DISCREPANCY I WILL NOT GUESS PAST. I have been told the board shows SignatureSuite as free. My read says it is held:

  rv-01M17C9M2JCD518HDWZBFZG4TF by codex-storymodel4s-scout, bead bd-01M17AS0BGAW9CF6VFHST9JMY3,
  covering signature.scala AND SignatureSuite.scala, UNTIL 20:25:16Z. It is 19:01Z.

So by my reading the scout holds both for another eighty minutes. I am not editing under that, and I am not assuming the other report is wrong either - one of us is misreading the board, and after today I would rather establish which than act on either belief. I have asked the scout directly.

If the discrepancy is in the TOOL rather than in either of our readings, that is worth knowing on its own - we have had three separate classes of silent mote failure today, and "in-flight disagrees with itself between actors" would be a fourth.

EVERYTHING ELSE ON THE BLEND IS DONE. 90c7ec0 on m1/blend-support: both wire reconstruction paths carry supportWeight, SensoryAbsenceSuite rewritten around the law rather than re-pinned, CostSuite 10/10 including both blend laws, rebased onto ae7f59e with movements RE-DERIVED and confirmed identical - your scout's change and mine are orthogonal, which I checked rather than assumed because I had predicted they might interact.

The two SignatureSuite literals are the only thing between this and a candidate. Still owed after that: golden re-cut and the cross-platform gate.

And my deciding vote on per-cell is posted with the arithmetic - fixed W_ref = 3.35 gives chart-bearing cells a 13-23% DISCOUNT, which is our own defect with the sign flipped, and on a chart-bearing corpus it collapses every row to Source. No constant works; the reference has to depend on what the cell could measure.
